title: Rainfall as IV for agricultural loan demand

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Two-stage least squares (2SLS) IV with cross-sectional data.
- Rationale: Credit (x) is likely endogenous in the yield equation due to reverse causality and omitted variables. Annual rainfall deviation (z) shifts credit demand but, by assumption, affects crop yield (y) only through credit, not directly.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0. Test via first-stage coefficient on z and F-statistic.
  - Exclusion: Conditional on controls, rainfall deviations affect yield only through their effect on credit, not via other channels (e.g., direct agronomic effects).
  - Independence: z is as-good-as-random with respect to unobserved determinants of y, conditional on controls.
  - Linearity/SUTVA: The structural relation is linear in logs and potential outcomes are well-defined.
  - With binary z: the 2SLS estimand is a LATE for households whose credit responds monotonically to rainfall; no defiers (monotonicity).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Packages
pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
to_install <- pkgs[!(pkgs %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(to_install)) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)
  library(sandwich)
  library(lmtest)
})

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s19_data.csv")

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("y","x","z","controls") %in% names(df)))
n <- nrow(df)
cat("Sample size:", n, "\n\n")

# Helper: print IV result with robust SE
print_iv_result <- function(ivfit, label){
  vc <- vcovHC(ivfit, type = "HC1")
  ct <- coeftest(ivfit, vcov = vc)
  est <- coef(ivfit)["x"]
  se  <- sqrt(vc["x","x"])
  ci  <- as.numeric(est + c(-1.96, 1.96)*se)
  cat(label, "\n")
  cat("  2SLS coefficient on x (elasticity):", round(est, 3),
      "  Robust SE:", round(se, 3),
      "  95% CI: [", round(ci[1], 3), ",", round(ci[2], 3), "]\n\n")
}

# 0) Naive OLS for comparison
ols_main <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_vc   <- vcovHC(ols_main, type = "HC1")
ols_ct   <- coeftest(ols_main, vcov = ols_vc)
ols_est  <- coef(ols_main)["x"]
ols_se   <- sqrt(ols_vc["x","x"])
ols_ci   <- as.numeric(ols_est + c(-1.96, 1.96)*ols_se)
cat("Naive OLS (y ~ x + controls):\n")
cat("  OLS coefficient on x:", round(ols_est, 3),
    "  Robust SE:", round(ols_se, 3),
    "  95% CI: [", round(ols_ci[1], 3), ",", round(ols_ci[2], 3), "]\n\n")

# 1) First stage: x on z and controls
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_sum <- summary(fs)
beta_z <- fs_sum$coefficients["z","Estimate"]
t_z    <- fs_sum$coefficients["z","t value"]
F_z    <- as.numeric(t_z^2)  # with one instrument, F = t^2
corr_xz <- cor(df$x, df$z)
cat("First stage (x ~ z + controls):\n")
cat("  Coefficient on z:", round(beta_z, 3),
    "  t-stat:", round(t_z, 2),
    "  First-stage F (excluded instrument):", round(F_z, 2), "\n")
cat("  Corr(x, z):", round(corr_xz, 3), "\n")
if(F_z < 10){
  cat("  WARNING: First-stage F < 10 (potential weak instrument).\n")
}
cat("\n")

# 2) Main IV (2SLS): y ~ x + controls | controls + z
iv_main <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = df, x = TRUE, y = TRUE)
print_iv_result(iv_main, "Main IV (y ~ x + controls | controls + z)")

# Diagnostics (non-robust, for reference; AER provides standard tests)
diag_main <- summary(iv_main, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("IV diagnostics (non-robust):\n")
print(diag_main$diagnostics)
cat("\n")

# 3) Robustness checks

# 3a) IV without controls: y ~ x | z
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
print_iv_result(iv_noc, "Robustness: IV without controls (y ~ x | z)")

# 3b) Add nonlinearity in controls: controls^2
df$controls2 <- df$controls^2
iv_quad <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls2 | controls + controls2 + z, data = df)
print_iv_result(iv_quad, "Robustness: IV with quadratic control (y ~ x + controls + controls^2 | ...)")

# 3c) Report OLS again to compare with IV (already printed)

# 4) Clear numerical takeaway (main result)
vc_main <- vcovHC(iv_main, type = "HC1")
est_main <- coef(iv_main)["x"]
se_main  <- sqrt(vc_main["x","x"])
ci_main  <- as.numeric(est_main + c(-1.96, 1.96)*se_main)
cat("=== Summary ===\n")
cat("Main 2SLS elasticity (y wrt x):", round(est_main, 3),
    "  Robust SE:", round(se_main, 3),
    "  95% CI: [", round(ci_main[1], 3), ",", round(ci_main[2], 3), "]\n")
cat("First-stage F-stat on instrument z:", round(F_z, 2), "\n")
cat("================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Higher credit availability should raise input use and facilitate smoothing and investment, increasing yields.
- Magnitude: Because both variables are in logs, the coefficient is an elasticity. A plausible magnitude is around 0.2–0.4. I expect roughly 0.3, smaller than or comparable to the naive OLS due to attenuation of upward bias from reverse causality or downward bias from measurement error, depending on which dominates.
- First-stage: Positive relevance of rainfall for loans (z → x), with a sufficiently large F-stat (>10) if the instrument is strong.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: rainfall; first stage: rainfall → loans; exclusion restriction: rainfall ⊥ yield | credit
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit access significantly increases crop yields
_ground_truth.main_effect: 10% increase in credit → 4% yield increase (IV estimate)
